subject: Evening surge: WebSocket/SSE jitter causing p95/p99 regressions - Brightline
messages:
From: Julie Barnes <julie@brightline.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.example>
Cc: ops-team@brightline.com
Date: 2028-05-14T17:12:00-07:00
Subject: Spike in streaming latency & dropped messages during evening peak

Hi Irene,

We started seeing a noticeable jump in user-visible latency on our live chat (SSE and websocket flows) beginning ~16:50 PDT. p95 is up from ~140ms to ~480ms and p99 is spiking above 1.8s. In the same window we see intermittent connection resets for ~2-3% of sessions. This is hitting our checkout assistance flow — carts are timing out and CS is swamped.

Attached are session logs and a short handshake trace from one client. We've already enabled local retry/backoff but that only masks the symptom. Can you triage? This is urgent for our evening peak.

Files attached: session-logs-20280514.tar.gz, sse-handshake-trace-17-05-14.txt

Thanks,
Julie
Julie Barnes
Head of Customer Ops — Brightline Retail
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.example>
To: Julie Barnes <julie@brightline.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example, aditya_rao@redwood.example, david_kim@redwood.example
Date: 2028-05-14T17:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in streaming latency & dropped messages during evening peak

Julie — thanks for the quick signal and attachments. I'm escalating to engineering and SRE immediately (cc'd).

Short plan while we triage:
- We will enable a temporary routing fallback to the dedicated pool and route a small percentage (~15%) of your traffic to reduce pressure on the hosted cluster.
- Recommend you keep client-side exponential backoff enabled for 2 retries and a 500ms base delay.
- We'll investigate whether KV cache heating or batching windows are contributing to tail latency.

Aditya / David: can you prioritize a dashboard check (queue depth, host queuing, kernel qdisc stats) for the last two hours and propose mitigations we can flip quickly?

Marissa: please open a high-priority CS ticket and coordinate a quick sync with Brightline ops — they requested an ETA and will want communications to stakeholders.

I'll update Julie within 30 minutes with next steps and ETA for an on-call runbook if needed.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.example>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.example>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: 2028-05-14T17:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in streaming latency & dropped messages during evening peak

Quick triage notes (observed 16:45 - 17:20 PDT):
- Host-level queue depth increased on a subset of hosts (gpuhost-17/18) servicing Brightline routes; average queue wait rose from 6ms to 42ms.
- KV cache miss rate increased ~4x for brightline model shard; we're seeing more model-weights paging on quantized paths during long sessions.
- Batching window for the streaming runtime currently set to 20ms; during peak it is allowing high queueing when requests burst.
- We also saw elevated WebSocket ACK delays and an increased number of half-open handshakes in the handshake trace.

Immediate mitigations we can push (low risk):
1) Reduce batch window from 20ms -> 5ms for Brightline routing policy (hotfix) — should drop queuing tail.
2) Temporarily divert 15% traffic to dedicated pool (Irene can approve).
3) Enable prefix KV warming for their high-frequency keys for 30 minutes.

I'll prepare a small hotfix to change the batching window and confidence-check on canary hosts. Attaching hotfix-reduce-batch-window.diff. Expect a 20-30 minute canary roll from approval.

Risks: slightly higher CPU per token on canary due to smaller batch efficiency but should reduce p99.

— Aditya (SRE/Serving Runtime)
From: Julie Barnes <julie@brightline.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.example>
Cc: ops-team@brightline.com
Date: 2028-05-14T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in streaming latency & dropped messages during evening peak

Irene / team — thanks for the rapid response. Please proceed with the following:
- Divert the 15% routing immediately.
- Apply the batch-window hotfix as a canary and let us know when it's live.

We tried increasing client retries but it only made client-side UX worse. We will stand down retries if you think server-side mitigation will hold. We also need an ETA for a full fix and a timeline for a postmortem and credits for customer impact.

We're available for a 30-minute bridge if you want to talk through steps — propose 18:30 PDT.

— Julie
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.example>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.example>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example, aditya_rao@redwood.example, david_kim@redwood.example
Date: 2028-05-15T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Exec summary: Brightline evening peak streaming p99 regressions — action & ask

Naomi — brief summary and asks for exec attention: 

What happened: Brightline experienced a sustained p95/p99 tail during evening peak on our hosted streaming endpoints (SSE/WebSocket). Impact: visible latency and ~2-3% connection resets affecting paid checkout-assist flows. Customer has active production traffic in US region.

Action taken so far:
- CS notified and on bridge with customer (Marissa).
- Diverted 15% of traffic to dedicated pool as temporary relief.
- Engineering pushed a canary hotfix that reduces the batching window (20ms -> 5ms) on selected shards; initial canary shows p99 improvement from ~1.8s -> ~650ms for canary traffic.
- Enabled KV warming for hot keys.

Ask:
- Approve offering a goodwill credit (recommend 10% of May usage) to Brightline if we observe a sustained customer-impact window of >30 minutes.
- If approved, Marissa will own external comms; I'll coordinate postmortem and timeline.

Next steps: finish canary rollout (target +60 min), run a 4-hour regression watch, and publish a brief postmortem to Brightline and internal ops.

I'll keep you posted on canary rollback/status.

— Irene
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
